findings.produced: GroupChatOrchestrator::with_database and GroupChatExecutor::with_database (builder methods setting the optional StateDatabase persistence path)
findings.rationale: rg -n "with_database" src/ interfaces/ shared/ returns only the two definitions — zero callers anywhere, not even tests. The only production construction sites (src/bin/aleph-server/commands/start/mod.rs:2713, 2728) call GroupChatOrchestrator::new and GroupChatExecutor::new(...).with_coordinator_visible(...) without with_database, so the db field is always None (orchestrator.rs:44, executor.rs:54) and every persistence branch is unreachable at runtime: create_session's insert_group_chat_session (orchestrator.rs:140-152), end_session's update_group_chat_session_status (orchestrator.rs:204-213), and executor::persist_turn (executor.rs:117-138, early return at :125). The group_chat_sessions/group_chat_turns tables (state_database/schema.rs:242,256) are created by migration but never written; sessions and turns survive only in memory. The prior review's owner_user_id persistence gap (review-results/group_chat.md) was fixed at the SQL layer (column + migration + insert param) but the fix is moot because the wire is missing.
findings.proposed_change: In src/bin/aleph-server/commands/start/mod.rs near line 2713/2728, pass the available StateDatabase Arc into both builders: GroupChatOrchestrator::new(gc_config, &persona_configs).with_database(db.clone()) and GroupChatExecutor::new(handle).with_coordinator_visible(...).with_database(db.clone()). Verify the local StateDatabase variable name at that construction site first.
findings.risk: Enables DB writes for the first time; persist_turn uses spawn_blocking per turn (executor.rs:117-138) and has zero test coverage via with_database, so wiring it exposes the SQLite path to real contention. Behavioral change: sessions/turns become durable across restart.
findings.verification: rg -n "with_database" src/ interfaces/ shared/ (only the 2 definitions); rg -n "GroupChatOrchestrator::new|GroupChatExecutor::new" src/ (production sites: start/mod.rs:2713/2728).
findings.existing_review_ref: review-results/group_chat.md (owner_user_id persistence gap, high) — SQL layer fixed, wire still missing; re-verified against current code.

findings.rationale: rg -n "with_provider_registry" src/ interfaces/ shared/ — production calls none; only definition + two test uses. The builder (start/mod.rs:2718-2729) snapshots reg.default_provider() into a StaticDefault and never passes a registry, so resolve_provider (executor.rs:89-114) always uses the default provider and Persona.provider / PersonaConfig.provider (protocol.rs:67, config/types/group_chat.rs:105-110) is an inert config knob with zero runtime effect; the provider_fallback_warned dedupe set (executor.rs:44-46) can never fill. Type seam: with_provider_registry takes Arc<crate::providers::ProviderRegistry> (struct, src/providers/registry.rs:35) while production holds MultiProviderRegistry (src/thinker/mod.rs:202) implementing the separate crate::thinker::ProviderRegistry trait (src/thinker/mod.rs:55) — an adapter or widened parameter is required.
findings.proposed_change: CONNECT — hand the executor a real provider registry at construction (start/mod.rs:2718-2729), preferring the live MultiProviderRegistry as both default handle and per-persona lookup source; adapt providers::ProviderRegistry vs thinker::ProviderRegistry type mismatch first.
findings.risk: Medium — activating per-persona provider overrides changes which provider serves persona turns; misconfigured persona providers would emit the fallback warn (previously impossible since the registry was never set).
findings.verification: rg -n "with_provider_registry" src/ interfaces/ shared/ — only executor.rs:66 (def) and :897/:1069 (tests, confirmed inside mod tests).

findings.consumer_location: none in production — constructed only in #[cfg(test)] (protocol.rs:477); matched by unreachable arms at src/gateway/inbound_router/group_chat_handler.rs:86, :102
findings.rationale: rg -n "GroupChatRequest::" src/ shows the only producers are channel.rs (Start at :105, End at :41 — parse_group_chat_command never emits Continue/Mention), tests, and the router match. The Continue/Mention match arms in group_chat_handler.rs:86-112 are provably unreachable. The RPC layer (handlers/group_chat.rs:191,294) implements continue/mention by parsing params directly, not via GroupChatRequest. Options: cut variants + arms (RPC covers the feature, channel auto-routes plain messages to active sessions at group_chat_handler.rs:113-150), or extend the parser — redundant and lacks session-map context.
findings.proposed_change: DECIDE — cut the two router arms (safe now, provably dead); enum variant removal deferred because the variants carry Serialize/Deserialize/JsonSchema derives (protocol.rs:125-165) forming a serializable contract.
findings.risk: Low — arms are unreachable; variant removal would change the serialized request schema.
